title: Higher direct images along a morphism of sites are sheafified cohomology presheaves
statement: Let $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), $f_*=u^s$, and let $R^qf_*:\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ ($q\ge0$) be the right derived functors of the left exact functor $f_*$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $R^qf_*\mathcal F=\mathcal H^q(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$ (cohomology computed in the abelian category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$) for an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For $\mathcal F\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $q\ge0$ let $\mathcal P^q_{\mathcal F}$ be the presheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal D$ with $\mathcal P^q_{\mathcal F}(V)=H^q(u(V),\mathcal F)=H^q(\mathcal I^\bullet(u(V)))$ ($H^q$ over an object, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)), the restriction along $V'\to V$ being induced by the restriction maps $\mathcal I^\bullet(u(V))\to\mathcal I^\bullet(u(V'))$. Then the canonical map of presheaves $\mathcal P^q_{\mathcal F}\to R^qf_*\mathcal F$ (sending the class of a cocycle $s\in\mathcal I^q(u(V))=(f_*\mathcal I^q)(V)$ to the section of the cohomology sheaf it defines) identifies $R^qf_*\mathcal F$ with the sheafification $(\mathcal P^q_{\mathcal F})^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; in particular $R^qf_*\mathcal F=0$ if and only if $(\mathcal P^q_{\mathcal F})^\#=0$.

proof.text: Use the given injective resolution I. Mathlib InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj identifies the homology of the pushed-forward cocomplex with the right derived object. The abelian sheaf categories and enough-injectives instances are supplied by Mathlib; no separate construction of a resolution or degree-zero calculation is required.

The statement already writes the presheaf as the homology of the underlying pushed-forward complex, and its sheafification comparison as the inverse of ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso for presheafToSheaf. Exactness of sheafification supplies this isomorphism. Thus no additional objectwise evaluation or construction of a cocycle comparison is needed for this Lean statement.

Mathlib sheafification_reflective makes the sheafification adjunction counit a natural isomorphism. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex to its asIso to obtain a natural isomorphism on cochain complexes. Its hom is definitionally NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex of the counit. Register its IsIso instance locally. Every component is therefore an isomorphism, and the homology functor maps the relevant component to an isomorphism.

The displayed morphism is a composite of the inverse homology-comparison isomorphism, the homology image of the counit isomorphism, and the inverse resolution isomorphism. The composite-isomorphism instance proves the conclusion. This holds in every degree, including zero, and for zero objects.

Not a Mathlib leaf: Mathlib has the pushforward of sheaves and Sheaf.cohomologyPresheaf but no right derived functors of pushforward and no sheafified-homology comparison (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep recorded). Proof split in five steps following the proof of 072W: (1) f_* left exact additive, injective resolution, R^q f_* F = H^q(f_*I); (2) presheaf cohomology of f_*I is P^q, via sectionwise exactness of evaluation; (3) construction of the canonical map theta from the left exactness of the inclusion iota; (4) sheafification is exact and its counit is an isomorphism, so H^q(f_*I) = (P^q)^# and the adjunct of theta is this isomorphism (written out: the source's 'by definition of the abelian category structure'); (5) vanishing. All cited nodes exist (Mathlib leaves except def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, same unit); no new nodes.
